emails.subject_b: quick question about client data at RBV Financial
emails.body:
Quick question for whoever handles this at RBV Financial: between the credit repair work, the tax prep, and the secure portal clients log into, is there a written information security plan covering all of it?

This is the kind of thing that tends to surface around EFIN or PTIN renewal time, or when a client asks how their data is handled, so it's worth having settled before it comes up.

I run Clear Path Secure, flat-rate IT and security work for tax and financial firms. I help firms get that plan documented and the basics locked down, without hiring IT staff. If someone else handles this, just point me their way.

Following up with the short version, since a vague "let me know" email isn't much use to anyone.

What's usually expected: a written plan for protecting client data, someone named as responsible for it, multi-factor authentication on email and the portal, and a plan for what happens if something goes wrong.

[[APPROVED]]

Between the credit reports you're pulling and the tax returns you're filing, RBV Financial is handling data that touches both of those responsibilities. Most firms have pieces of this in place already, just not written down in one document. Curious where things stand on your end.

I put together a one-page checklist that lays out what's usually expected, in plain language, so you can see where RBV Financial stands in about ten minutes. No call needed to use it.

Want me to send it over?

emails.subject_a: a founding-client offer for RBV Financial
emails.body:
I'm taking on a small group of Ohio firms right now, and part of that is a free security audit for founding clients. In exchange I get honest feedback as I build this out, which matters more to me than what I'd normally charge for it.

If that's useful for RBV Financial, happy to grab 15 minutes: {{booking_link}}. And if tax season timing is bad right now, just tell me when to check back and I will.

Either way, no pressure.

Haven't heard back, so I'll take that as "not right now," and that's fine.

If a written security plan ever comes up, from a client, a partner, or your own planning, just reply here and I'll send that checklist over.

Hope filing season goes smoothly for you.
